From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 13 May 2027 08:05:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Demo request — scheduling link shows wrong timezone for Tokyo users

Hi Akira / Olga —

Quick technical note from the integrations side: Calendly normally detects timezone from the browser but it will fall back to the account/organization setting or to a query param if supplied. Two immediate options we recommend:

1) Force the timezone on the public link: append "?tz=Asia/Tokyo" to the Calendly URL. That forces displayed times into JST regardless of the prospect's machine settings.

2) For Chili Piper, the equivalent is to add the "locale" parameter (e.g., "locale=ja_JP") and/or pass a timezone in the event metadata payload.

We also confirmed this particular bug is a mismatch introduced during a routing change — some links omit the tz param when generated via our outreach templates. We'll patch the template today and reissue fresh links for affected accounts.

Note on DST: Japan doesn't observe DST, so Asia/Tokyo will remain stable. For future APAC regions that do have DST (Australia, NZ) we'll add an automated check into our scheduling helper to surface potential DST offsets in the UI.

Olga — I'll follow up once the template is updated and will paste a force-link you can use in emails.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Integrations Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
